title: Cache coherence glitch — customer brief & verification playbook
body:
TL;DR: On 2029-10-11 07:14 UTC we observed a partial degradation affecting a subset of tenants where recent requests returned stale completions (older prefixes). The root cause was a cache-coherence bug that caused KV cache shards to be misrouted after autoscaling events. Impact was limited to ~0.8% of requests for affected tenants over a 42-minute window. We rolled back the autoscaler change, forced a cache flush, and deployed a targeted routing fix. This note explains what happened, who may be affected, what we did, and how customers can verify and recover if they saw anomalous outputs.

What happened (customer-facing):
- Symptom: Some API calls returned completions that incorporated content or prefixes from earlier unrelated requests. This happened intermittently and only for sessions routed through autoscaled GPU shards during a brief window.
- Surface impact: Stale or semantically incorrect continuations (e.g., response referencing earlier conversation turn, mismatched context), not data exfiltration. No customer data was leaked across tenant boundaries; the issue was caused by stale KV cache entries being reused within the same tenant routing path.

Who may be affected:
- Affected: Tenants using hosted API with per-request routing to autoscaled shared pools between 07:14 and 07:56 UTC on 2029-10-11. Tenants with high-concurrency streaming workloads and long-lived sessions were slightly more likely to see the symptom.
- Not affected: Dedicated/reserved pools (no autoscaling event), private on-prem deployments, and embedding-only workload patterns.

Technical root cause (summary):
- During an autoscale-up event we introduced a race between shard registration and the KV cache assignment table. In a narrow timing window the router assigned requests to a newly added shard before its KV cache pointer table replicated the latest assignment map. As a result, some requests read from an outdated KV cache index and reused prefix state from a previously retired shard instance.
- Important clarifications:
  - Tenant isolation remained intact: cache keys are namespaced by tenant and model version, so we did not observe cross-tenant data mixing.
  - The issue is coherence (stale pointer/assignment), not serialization or durability.

Timeline (UTC):
- 07:12: monitoring alert: small increase in prefix-mismatch error rate in EU region.
- 07:14: on-call SRE escalated after automated sampling detected stale prefix reuse in traces.
- 07:18: engineering disabled the new autoscaler change and began rolling back the configuration.
- 07:26: we initiated a forced KV cache flush for affected autoscaled pools and disabled shard warm-start.
- 07:38: patch to router assignment logic deployed to EU pool (hotfix). Observed steady reduction in anomalies.
- 07:56: metric baseline restored; monitoring remained green after continued observation.
- 08:30: post-incident validation run; longer-term fix PR opened (linked above).

Mitigations performed (what we did):
- Immediate: Disabled the autoscaling configuration that triggered the race; forced KV cache invalidation for pools active during the window; applied conservative routing to fall back to non-autoscaled warm nodes for latency-critical sessions.
- Short-term: Hotfix to guard shard registration and assignment replication ordering (deployed and validated); increased monitoring sensitivity for prefix coherence and added an alert for assignment replication lag >50ms.
- Long-term: Scheduled a defensive redesign of the shard registration handshake (PR in progress) and added additional unit/integration tests that simulate concurrent registration + routing.

Customer verification checklist (how you can check if you were affected):
1) Check your request logs for the window 2029-10-11 07:14–07:56 UTC (region: EU/Europe). Look for responses that reference prior conversation text that was not sent as part of the recent request. Example query pattern to search logs:
   - "response includes 'previous turn' OR 'earlier message' OR 'context:' AND request_timestamp between 2029-10-11T07:14:00Z and 2029-10-11T07:56:00Z"
2) Use the request_id in traces to ask us for the collected runtime trace. If you have request IDs where you suspect stale output, send them to support with this subject line: "INC-2127 suspected stale-output — request-ids".
3) Verify sequence continuity in streaming sessions: look for repeated token sequences or unexpected context resets.

Recovery / replay options we offer:
- Option A: We can run a deterministic replay of specific request_ids against a clean runtime with flushed caches and provide you both the replay outputs and diff against the live response. This is recommended if you need to verify correctness for a sample of requests.
- Option B (bulk): For customers with larger exposure who opt in, we can run an offline bulk replay for specific time ranges using your signed consent and provide a report summarizing mismatch rates and recommended remediations.
- Option C: If your app logged user-visible outputs and you prefer, we can provide a replay evidence bundle (see below) so you can reconcile outputs offline.

Evidence package we can provide (what you'll receive if you request it):
- Per-request replay artifacts: original request payload, live response, deterministic replay output, runtime trace, and token-level parity diff.
- Aggregate metrics for your tenant for the window (request count, mismatch rate, percentile latency before/after fix).
- Signed integrity statement showing namespace/key mapping and assurance that tenant isolation maintained.

How to request the evidence kit (steps):
1) Open a support ticket and include: organization name, tenant id, requested time window (default: 07:14–07:56 UTC), and up to 25 sample request_ids (if available).
2) Select desired level: sample replay (fast), bulk replay (longer; requires export consent), or evidence-only package.
3) Our CS team will share an encrypted S3 location for results; expect 24–72 hours for sample replays and up to 7 business days for large bulk jobs.

Short-term customer guidance (if you saw an issue):
- If you saw a small number of anomalous responses: flag request_ids and request a sample replay. No code changes are required on your side.
- If you observed systematic misuse of context in a particular route: consider temporarily pinning that route to a dedicated (non-autoscaled) pool or lowering concurrency until we confirm full mitigation.
- If you require additional guardrails: enable per-session KV isolation option (available as an opt-in on per-tenant configs) — CS can toggle this for you during the verification window.

Preventative actions we are taking:
- Strengthen the shard registration handshake and add deterministic ordering guarantees for assignment propagation.
- Add chaos-tests in staging that simulate concurrent scale events while replaying long-lived sessions.
- Improve our real-time detection to surface prefix-coherence anomalies faster and wire them to automated mitigations.

Customer impact summary (numbers):
- Estimated affected requests: ~0.8% of requests for impacted tenants during the window.
- Number of tenants with at least one recorded anomaly: 14 (out of ~1,800 active hosted tenants in EU at that time).
- No reports of data leakage; no cross-tenant key exposure detected.

Contact & next steps:
- If you want a replay or evidence package, please open a support ticket referencing INC-2127 and include any request_ids.
- We will follow up proactively with customers who generated anomalous traces in our sampling set.
- A full technical postmortem will be published on Confluence once the long-term fix ships (target: two weeks).

Apology and assurance:
We understand that correctness matters. We're sorry for the disruption and are treating this with high priority. The fixes we deployed reduce the probability of recurrence significantly; the long-term changes will further harden the system against this class of race.

Appendix: sample log query (internal but shareable with customers who have logging access):
- Kibana: index=runtime-logs-*, tenant_id=YOUR_TENANT_ID AND @timestamp:[2029-10-11T07:14:00Z TO 2029-10-11T07:56:00Z] AND message:/prefix-mismatch|kv-cache-read/ | sort @timestamp desc

Appendix: quick validation curl (customer-friendly):
- If you captured a request_id and want a quick check, run: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/internal/trace?request_id=<REQUEST_ID>"
  (Support will only expose traces for your tenant after auth checks.)

Prepared by: Aisha Patel (Customer Success) with engineering and SRE support.
